title: Point images, continuity, and open embeddings for algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Use algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], their field-valued point classes and atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], and open subspaces [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. For arbitrary morphisms $a:A\to B$ and $c:C\to B$, the map $|A\times_BC|\to |A|\times_{|B|}|C|$ is surjective, and $\operatorname{im}(|A\times_BC|\to|C|)=|c|^{-1}(\operatorname{im}|a|)$; fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A representable map $a:A\to B$ is surjective on every scheme base change if and only if $|a|$ is surjective. Every morphism of algebraic spaces induces a continuous point map. If it is representable etale, its point map is open. For an open subspace $j:J\hookrightarrow B$, $|j|$ is injective and identifies $|J|$ homeomorphically with an open subset of $|B|$. For any scheme atlas $p:U\to B$, the inverse image of that subset is the underlying open of $U\times_BJ$. If $J_1,J_2\subseteq B$ are open subspaces, then $|J_1|\subseteq|J_2|$ if and only if $J_1\subseteq J_2$ as subfunctors. In particular an open subspace with full point image equals $B$.

proof.text: Prove the common-field relation of [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes] is an equivalence. For transitivity of p~q and q~r, form the scheme pullback of the two common-field spectra over the spectrum of q's field. Their unique points have the same image; [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-pullback-compatible-point] gives a point of the pullback. Its residue-field spectrum maps to both common fields compatibly over the middle field and the base, so restricting both equalities gives p~r. Thus equality in Quot is actual common-field agreement. Identify ordinary scheme points with Yoneda point classes: a representative maps to the image of its unique point, and [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field] factors it through that image's residue field. Common-field agreement preserves the ordinary image, proving injectivity and surjectivity, naturally in scheme morphisms.

For any presheaf pullback square, choose field representatives of two compatible point classes. Step 1 gives a common field on which their images agree. Yoneda turns the restricted sections into compatible maps from that field spectrum; the categorical pullback lift defines a representative projecting to both classes. The sheaf-to-presheaf functor preserves pullbacks, so this applies to the displayed sheaf pullback of algebraic spaces. Commutativity gives one inclusion in the projection-image formula, and the compatible-pair lift gives the other.

proof.text: For any representable map, its representing scheme-test square has projection image equal to the inverse image of its point image: apply step 2 and the scheme-point bijections and naturality of step 1. If the map is point-surjective, this makes every test projection surjective. Conversely test a field representative using scheme-test surjectivity from [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Choose a point over the unique point of the field spectrum; its residue-field representative maps to the original class. Hence scheme-test surjectivity and point-surjectivity agree.

source.place: Tag 03H5 (lemma-characterize-surjective), same argument with arbitrary representable source.

proof.text: Compare the topology in [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover] with the final topology of [def-a1-space-point-topology]. All etale tests are continuous for the former; its atlas is itself one of the latter's tests. The two topology inequalities give equality. The scheme-source continuity clause then proves continuity for every map from an arbitrary presheaf to an algebraic space: on every etale scheme test of the source, the composite point map is the continuous scheme point map to the target. Use the final-topology criterion.

For a representable etale map to B choose a surjective etale scheme atlas W→B. Its pullback is represented by V with an etale scheme projection i:V→W. The other map q:h_V→A is representable etale and surjective: test the corresponding properties of W→B on a composite scheme test, and use pullback cancellation. Its point map is continuous by the final-topology definition and surjective by the residue-field construction of step 3. The composite |f|∘|q|=|w|∘|i| is open, since i is etale and the atlas point map is open by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. An open composite descends along the continuous surjection |q|, proving openness of |f|. This also applies when A is an arbitrary presheaf.

source.place: Tag 03IR (lemma-etale-open), scheme-atlas reduction; morphisms.tex Tags 02GN (lemma-composition-etale) and 02GP (lemma-open-immersion-etale).

proof.text: An open-subfunctor inclusion is representable etale: its scheme tests are open immersions by [def-a1-space-open-subspace], hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1). It is injective on point classes because common-field equality in the ambient functor already holds in the subfunctor. Steps 4 and 5 therefore make it a continuous open injection, hence an open embedding. On any scheme atlas its representing square is an open immersion by definition, and step 3 identifies its ordinary image with the inverse image of the point image.

source.place: Tags 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces, topology of the inclusion), 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian), and 03IR (lemma-etale-open).

proof.text: Subfunctor inclusion implies point-image inclusion by composing representatives. Conversely take any section of J1 over T and pull the open subfunctor J2 back to T. By step 3 every ordinary point of T is in the image of the representing open immersion, because its residue-field class lies in J1 and hence in J2. The open immersion is therefore surjective and is an isomorphism by [def-weil-open-immersion]. Its inverse lifts the original section into J2. This proves subfunctor inclusion objectwise without requiring J1 to be open. Apply this argument with J1 the full subfunctor to prove that full point image forces J2 to be the full subfunctor.

source.place: Tag 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces), inclusion; Tag 03IE (lemma-factor-through-open-subspace), scheme-test argument for full point image.

X3 implements the relation equivalence via a scheme pullback, proves the presheaf point calculus directly, and descends openness from a target atlas.

split_report.summary: Seven-step split using only existing nodes. Compare scheme points with field-valued classes, construct compatible fibre-product points over a common field, derive representable surjectivity on all scheme tests, use the existing scheme-atlas theorem to obtain final-topology continuity, prove etale openness by an explicit composite scheme test, and prove open embeddings and inclusion by subfunctor injectivity and full-image open scheme tests. Statement and its dependencies are unchanged; no new nodes and no attachment. All cited statements and sources were read; searches run and logged, with scheme-only hits rejected.

lean.statement: theorem point_open_calculus {S : Scheme.{u}} : (∀ (A B C : AlgebraicSpace S) (a : A ⟶ B) (c : C ⟶ B), (∀ (x : Point A.obj.obj) (z : Point C.obj.obj), mapPoint a.hom.hom x = mapPoint c.hom.hom z → ∃ t : Point (Limits.pullback a.hom c.hom).obj, mapPoint (Limits.pullback.fst a.hom c.hom).hom t = x ∧ mapPoint (Limits.pullback.snd a.hom c.hom).hom t = z) ∧ pointImage (Limits.pullback.snd a.hom c.hom).hom = mapPoint c.hom.hom ⁻¹' pointImage a.hom.hom) ∧ (∀ (A B : AlgebraicSpace S) (a : A ⟶ B), IsRepresentable a.hom.hom → (IsSurjective a.hom.hom ↔ Function.Surjective (mapPoint a.hom.hom))) ∧ (∀ (A B : AlgebraicSpace S) (a : A ⟶ B), Continuous (mapPoint a.hom.hom)) ∧ (∀ (A B : AlgebraicSpace S) (a : A ⟶ B), IsEtale a.hom.hom → IsOpenMap (mapPoint a.hom.hom)) ∧ (∀ (B : AlgebraicSpace S) (J : OpenSubspace B), Topology.IsOpenEmbedding (mapPoint J.val.ι) ∧ ∀ (U : Over S) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ B.obj.obj), IsEtale p → IsSurjective p → ∃ (V : Over S) (i : V ⟶ U) (q : yoneda.obj V ⟶ J.val.toFunctor), IsPullback q (yoneda.map i) J.val.ι p ∧ IsOpenImmersion i.left ∧ schemePointMap p ⁻¹' pointImage J.val.ι = Set.range i.left) ∧ (∀ (B : AlgebraicSpace S) (J₁ J₂ : OpenSubspace B), pointImage J₁.val.ι ⊆ pointImage J₂.val.ι ↔ J₁.val ≤ J₂.val) ∧ (∀ (B : AlgebraicSpace S) (J : OpenSubspace B), pointImage J.val.ι = Set.univ → J.val = ⊤)
